item.title: Gilgeous-Alexander scores 30 points to lead the Thunder past the Mavericks, 100-87
item.description: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 30 points, Chet Holmgren had 19 points and nine rebounds and the Oklahoma City Thunder beat the Dallas Mavericks 100-87 on Sunday night.

item.title: Catherine O'Hara wins posthumous award for 'The Studio' at Actor Awards
item.description: A month after her unexpected death, Catherine O'Hara won a posthumous award at the 32nd Actor Awards for her performance on "The Studio."

item.title: Queta's career-high 27 points spark Celtics to 114-98 win over 76ers
item.description: Neemias Queta scored a career-high 27 points and added 17 rebounds to help the Boston Celtics recover from a slow start and rally past the Philadelphia 76ers 114-98.

item.title: Baldwin boys basketball team reaches Nassau Class AAA final
item.description: Loss by Farmingdale ends coach Jim Pastier's 24-year run.

item.title: What to know about Iran's Revolutionary Guard, a powerful force within the country's theocracy
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard has become a powerful force within the country's theocracy, answering only to the supreme leader.

item.title: San Diego's Dreyer, Ingvartsen, Ferree deliver 2-0 victory over St. Louis City
item.description: Anders Dreyer and Marcus Ingvartsen both had a goal and an assist, and rookie teenager Duran Ferree earned his second clean sheet in his second start when San Diego FC finished off a 2-0 victory over St. Louis City.

item.title: Clippers beat the Pelicans 137-117 to end a 3-game losing streak
item.description: Kawhi Leonard scored 23 points and the Los Angeles Clippers beat the New Orleans Pelicans 137-117 on Sunday night to end a three-game losing streak.

item.title: Gauthier scores 2 goals and Ducks edge Flames 3-2 in shootout for 8th straight home win
item.description: Cutter Gauthier scored twice in regulation, Leo Carlsson and Mason McTavish both converted in the shootout, and the Anaheim Ducks beat the Calgary Flames 3-2.

item.title: Luka and LeBron lead Lakers past Kings 128-104 to complete back-to-back weekend wins
item.description: Luka Doncic had 28 points and nine assists, LeBron James added 24 points and the Los Angeles Lakers finished a back-to-back set with a 128-104 victory over the Sacramento Kings.
